title: finding(plugin-detail): an authored `aria` name on `record:activity` / `record:chatter` nests OUTSIDE the panel's own region, so the panel a user hears is still the built-in name
body:
Dedupe keywords: nested named regions · `record:activity` · `record:chatter` · `RecordActivityTimeline` · `RecordChatterPanel` · authored aria name · two landmarks

Filed by the `domain:ui` execution seat (seat 3) out of the isolated at-tier contract review of PR objectui#9935 (card objectui#9556), which escalated it as **outside that card's file surface**. ⛔ Unassigned, ungraded, ⛔ no `domain:*` — routing is the triage seat's.

Filed-by: `session_01Xm4WFhEe5mwcgyqHjxR2hn` (`domain:ui` seat 3, seat post objectui#9800)

## The shape

PR objectui#9935 makes six record blocks honour the `aria` bag the protocol declares. On `record:activity` and `record:chatter` that produces **two named regions, nested**: the authored name lands on the block's **outer container**, while the panel component inside keeps **its own** built-in section name.

⚠️ So an author who writes `aria: { ariaLabel: 'Deal history' }` gets a region called *Deal history* wrapping a region called something else — and the name a screen-reader user hears **for the panel** is still the built-in one. ⭐ That is very likely ⛔ not what the author meant.

## What is measured, and what is not

- The nesting is **measured and pinned as shipped, ⛔ not as right**: the contract review confirms the pin's composition case is green at head, red on the base, and red under its own ablation leg B. Record comment `5734967234` on PR objectui#9935 (this seat re-read its `issue_url` before citing it).
- ⛔ **Not measured**: whether any real authored document hits this, and what a screen-reader user actually hears in either arrangement. No instance is claimed.

## Why it was not settled there

The alternative threads the authored name into `RecordActivityTimeline` / `RecordChatterPanel`, which are **outside** objectui#9556's file surface, carry their own accessibility pins, and have a host-mounted fallback path in `@object-ui/app-shell`. ⭐ The delivering dev shipped the measured arrangement and said plainly it was ⛔ not deciding the question; the review agreed that was correct and escalated it here.

## The options, as they stood when it was escalated

- **A — nest (shipped)**: the block's container takes the authored name, the panel keeps its built-in one. Two named regions. ⛔ No plumbing, and the panel's own name is never lost.
- **B — replace**: thread the authored name into the panel components so the panel's own section carries it. One region, probably what an author expects. Touches components with their own a11y pins and a host-mounted fallback.
- **C — nest, but mark the outer container `role='group'`** rather than `region`, so it is ⛔ not a landmark.

⚠️ These are recorded as the state of the question, ⛔ **not** as a decision box: this card is ordinary work, and whoever takes it should re-derive the options against the tree rather than inherit this list — ⭐ three cards this shift had their inherited lists falsified, each with a lit control behind them.

## Not measured

⛔ Whether `record:related_list`, `record:details` or `record:highlights` compose the same way — only the two panel-bearing blocks were named. ⛔ What WCAG or the repo's own a11y pins require here; neither was consulted when the arrangement was chosen, because the arrangement was a by-product rather than a choice.

Refs: objectui#9556 (the card) · PR objectui#9935 (where it shipped) · review record `5734967234` · objectui#9945 (the separate, maintainer-facing alias question out of the same review).
